## TL;DR

Built the native Hub and exercised the requested second-pass flows in a fresh QA registry. The File menu, Add Server sheet, server context menu and edit form, Cmd-K quick switcher, relaunch persistence, and both explicit Hub appearances behaved as expected. No code defect surfaced, so the pass adds an observed-results record rather than speculative source changes. Signed-in task search remains outside the evidence from this run because the embedded page was at sign-in; human QA task #1174 owns that view. The detailed QA record is `docs/qa/2026-11-macos-hub-second-pass.md`.

## Work and rationale

I first read the #1193 task and the previous macOS Hub QA record. That prior record documented an important isolation risk: a Hub process launched for QA can write server registry state unless `REPOOS_HUB_SUPPORT_DIRECTORY` is set. I used a new directory under `/Users/nick/Library/Caches/RepoOS/hub-qa-1193` for the entire manual pass and left the normal application registry untouched. I used a separate derived-data directory under the same cache root as well.

The Debug target built successfully with the macOS SDK and `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`. Xcode emitted a CoreDevice/CoreSimulator compatibility warning because the installed CoreSimulator framework is older than the framework expected by this Xcode. That warning did not prevent the macOS target from building or launching. The native XCTest run completed with 191 passed, 7 skipped, and 0 failed. XCTest emitted AppKit constraint-conflict runtime warnings from `HubFindBarContainerTests`; the interactive Cmd-K quick switcher did not show a corresponding visual or functional fault in this pass, so I recorded the warnings without inferring a product bug from them.

I launched the resulting app through LaunchServices, which opened the initial empty Hub window. The File menu exposed New RepoOS Window, Add Server, Close, and Close All. Add Server opened its native sheet, where Running locally discovered the live `repoos` service at `localhost:7171`. Choosing that row populated the address field; submitting Add server performed the health check and resulted in a selected, healthy sidebar entry.

I opened the server row’s context menu and confirmed the expected actions were present, including Copy URL and Edit server. The edit sheet exposed the display name, origin, optional group, SF Symbol, accent color, and pin controls. I changed the display name to `RepoOS QA` and group to `Second pass`, saved, and observed the new values in the sidebar with the server still healthy. These values were written only into the disposable QA registry.

I quit the Hub and relaunched the same built app with the same support-directory override. The sidebar restored `RepoOS QA` as selected and healthy. The JSON registry retained the edited name and group as well as the selected server ID. This verifies persistence across a normal app relaunch without relying on memory of the prior window.

The Settings window offered System, Light, and Dark Hub themes. I selected Light and Dark in turn and inspected both renderings. The controls and explanatory copy remained legible in both appearances. I captured the app windows using `screencapture -l<windowid>`; all PNGs remain in the cache directory and were not added to the repository.

Finally, I invoked `⌘K` from the main Hub window after relaunch. The quick switcher opened and contained the saved server, its recent contexts, and Add server. Searching for `repoos` returned the local matching entries. Searching for `1193` returned No matches. The embedded web view was at the sign-in page, so the last result establishes the empty-state behavior but cannot establish signed-in task search. The task itself points signed-in project/task validation to human-owned #1174, and I have not entered credentials or claimed that path passed.

## Approaches tried

I used a dedicated `xcodebuild` derived-data directory and launched the built `.app` through LaunchServices with an explicit support-directory environment override. This follows the app’s QA guidance and avoids letting a test run mutate the person’s everyday Hub registry. For manual interaction I used the native accessibility tree to inspect controls and menus, invoke buttons, enter the edit values, and verify the resulting state. Screenshots were taken only with the Hub window IDs, never as full-screen captures.

I also attempted the task query `1193` through the quick switcher. It returned No matches while the embedded server page was logged out. I retained this as an explicit limit rather than treating it as a successful signed-in search check or diagnosing it as a product bug without authenticated evidence.

## Challenges and blockers

The local Xcode installation reported that its simulator/device frameworks are mismatched. The output identified CoreSimulator `1051.55.0` as older than the build’s `1174.21.0` and also logged a CoreDevice symbol-loading error. This did not block the macOS build, the successful native test run, or the interactive app flow. XCTest also logged AppKit constraint-conflict warnings from the Hub find-bar container tests; these remain recorded for future investigation if they correspond to a reproducible UI fault.

The only functional boundary was authentication: the test server displayed its sign-in page, so this run did not have authenticated task results to search. Since #1193 says signed-in project/task views are tracked in #1174, I left that verification with the intended human task and did not use credentials or fabricate task-search evidence.

## Key learnings

The Hub’s first-run Add Server flow remains coherent when driven through the actual native sheet: discovery fills the origin, health is checked before saving, and the row appears as healthy. Context-menu editing persists identity and grouping changes through a full quit/relaunch. Cmd-K is reachable from the main window and presents local server and recent-context results even when the embedded web UI is not signed in. Explicit Light and Dark Hub settings remain readable; each applies to the native shell, while the embedded server UI keeps its own theme.

For future manual macOS QA, always give the Hub process a disposable `REPOOS_HUB_SUPPORT_DIRECTORY`, including when relaunching. Keep DerivedData and screenshot outputs outside the worktree. When a task explicitly separates signed-in verification into a human-owned task, record the authentication boundary precisely and avoid turning an unauthenticated empty result into a claim about task search.
